lines.text: A bug report comes in. Checkout fails on Safari, and someone has to deal with it.
Someone has to triage it, pick an agent, and then chase the fix, step by step.
Workflows chain agents with events. An event is a named signal, like bug triaged.
The triage workspace finishes its work, and emits the event, saying what happened.
That event is wired to the fixer workspace, and a new task appears there on its own.
Drag the workspaces onto events, and the graph draws itself. Triage, then fixer, then review.
The fixer is already listening, so it picks up the task the moment the signal arrives.
When the fix is ready, it emits its own event, and the review workspace wakes up.
All of it is visible on the graph, so you can see what fired what, and when.
Every workspace keeps its approvals, so a person still decides on the risky steps, like a merge.
Bug in, fix out. You only step in when a decision really needs you.
How many steps sit between a bug report and a fix on your team? Tell us below, then try Workflows at Agent R Q dot com.
